- Why: log text is not private.

`"Starte asynchrone E-Mail Verarbeitung"`, so translating that line blanks
the panels with no error anywhere. Changing one needs a coordinated infra PR.

- **Left, and frozen: 13 fully German prose lines** — 9 in
`EmbeddingStoreService`. These are prose, which is what rule 6 of
- **Done: 28 statements** that were *English sentences quoting a German term
`Analyse`, `Kunde=`). Rule 6's own carve-out already covered them — *"this
does not freeze identifier names quoted inside an otherwise-English log
line"* — so leaving them was a rule violation rather than a judgment call,

had taken the `Kunde`→`Client` rename but not `Ausschreibung`→`Tender`.

second recorded it but left it frozen. Hence counts rather than assertions.

message text. Neither literal appears in any of the 28. The matched line is

itself covered this file like any other, so ~135 lines of German prompt
were renamed for something that is about to be deleted.
likewise unused and can go with it.

## Reconcile the two contradicting rule blocks in RedFlagAgent
- Added: 2026-07-31 (found while scoping the German-to-English rename)

folgende AUSSCHLUSSKRITERIEN`) and again at L74-89 (`AUFGABE: Analysiere

Fixing it changes classification behaviour, so it wants its own PR with
eval coverage, not a rename PR.

## Repair or delete the eval fixtures under `src/test/resources/evals`
- Why: they look like a safety net and are not one. 16 of the 42 files are
empty; several expected outputs hold values that cannot bind to their
record types (`"startDate": "ab sofort"` and `"endDate": "null"` against a
`LocalDate`); and no code reads any of them — there is no harness, so
nothing fails when an expectation goes stale. The rename translated their
keys and directory names for consistency, which makes them look *more*
current than they are. Either build the harness that runs them (and fix
the type errors it would surface) or delete the tree; leaving inert
fixtures around invites the next person to trust them.
Note the `Input/` fixtures are raw freelancermap payloads and use
are deliberately not renamed, only the `ExpectedOutput/` ones mirror our
`find src/test/resources/evals -type f -empty` for the empty files and
`grep -rn "evals" src/test/java` for a reader. An empty first result and a
non-empty second means the fixtures are populated and actually executed.
Today that is 16 files and no reader. (Not `grep -rlx ""`: that matches an
empty *line*, and a 0-byte file has none, so it exits 1 and prints nothing
with all 16 sitting right there — a check that reports the opposite of the
truth is worse than no check.)
- Status: the script now runs as a `ci.yml` step, so the "nothing invokes it"
half of this entry is closed. What is left is the false-negative class
below, which no shell version can close.
- Why: renames move methods and types; javadoc `{@link}` targets do not
follow, and nothing in the Maven build notices. This PR shipped `{@link #von}`
pointing at a method renamed to `of`, and inherited `{@link Bearbeiter#name()}`
from `main` — a type that never existed — which the rename dutifully
translated to `{@link Assignee#name()}`, equally non-existent. The script
strips comments before resolving, so a link cannot satisfy itself out of
its own comment text, and it runs a positive control before every scan.
**A clean run is not coverage.** It has a known false-negative class:
resolution is `grep -w` over comment-stripped *text*, which still contains
every string literal, so a link is satisfied by its symbol appearing in any
string anywhere. Demonstrated — injecting the genuinely dangling
`@Operation(summary = "Assigns a Bearbeiter to the Ausschreibung by id")`
supplies the word. The one link it did catch, `{@link Assignee#name()}`,
was caught only because "Assignee" occurs zero times in any string literal.
Separating a declaration from a word in a string needs a parse, which shell
cannot do, so **this class is only closed by the real fix**: a
`-Xdoclint:reference`. Do that and delete the script.
That fix is a bigger job than it looks, which is why it is still here:
javadoc reads *unprocessed* sources, so it dies on Lombok before doclint
